about.details: Runs Antigravity, Google's agent-first desktop application for software development. It needs a Google account and network access to Google's services. Its build is linked against glibc, and it was made and tried on LevitateOS. It carries the desktop runtime (GTK, NSS, X11, GLib and the C library) inside its own package instead of using the host's, so the desktop image does not have to ship them; the package is about 600 MB. Its sandbox uses unprivileged user namespaces, since the setuid helper is not installed; a kernel without them stops it with an error. The program can check for newer versions through its bundled updater; updates are made by Recipe (recipe update antigravity), and the program's own update setting can be set to manual or none. The package is proprietary Google software.

about.details: The full FFmpeg codec library, so H.264, HEVC (H.265), AAC and the other formats this build of FFmpeg decodes start to play. They play in the programs that use the system's FFmpeg: Firefox for web video, Qt and KDE players, and the video thumbnails in the file manager. This does not add hardware decoding. Programs that play only through GStreamer need GStreamer's own plug-ins, which this does not bring. The system's own FFmpeg leaves these formats out because they are covered by patents in some countries; whether to install them is your choice, and you are responsible for it where you live. It also adds the libraries the full codec library needs: x264 (H.264 encoding), x265 (HEVC encoding) and vvenc (VVC/H.266 encoding), for programs that encode video through FFmpeg. It is RPM Fusion's libavcodec-freeworld with those libraries and numactl-libs from Fedora, fetched by this recipe from RPM Fusion and Fedora; LevitateOS does not redistribute it. It is open source software (GPL-3.0-or-later and the licences of the added libraries). It is built for exactly the system's FFmpeg version (9.0.2) and must match it: when a system release changes FFmpeg, this recipe is updated to the matching build. Built for glibc and LevitateOS; AcornOS (musl) already ships the full codecs.

about.details: Valve's Steam: the store, library and launcher for games, Counter-Strike 2 among them. This installs Valve's Steam launcher, the menu entry and icon, the device rules that let Steam controllers, other game pads and VR headsets work without root, and the 32-bit libraries Steam and its runtime load (the lib32 group). On first start the launcher downloads the Steam client from Valve into ~/.local/share/Steam. The Steam client updates itself there, from Valve, every time it starts, and it has no setting to turn that off: Recipe installs and updates the launcher, the device rules and the libraries, and the client and the games are Steam's own. Graphics: the system's own drivers are Mesa's (OpenGL and Vulkan, 64- and 32-bit), meant for AMD and Intel graphics; on NVIDIA they are nouveau and its Vulkan driver. For NVIDIA's proprietary driver, install its recipe, which must bring its 32-bit libraries too; that recipe is still to be written. Games run in Steam's runtime container (Steam Linux Runtime), which needs unprivileged user namespaces in the kernel. Needs a Steam account and network access to Valve. Steam is proprietary software under Valve's Steam Subscriber Agreement; the recipe downloads it from Valve and LevitateOS does not redistribute it. Built for glibc and LevitateOS; AcornOS (musl) cannot run it.
